why: Water above bar i is min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i]. With pointers at both ends, the side whose running max is smaller is the side whose water is already decided (the other side has a wall at least that tall), so settle that bar and move that pointer inward: move the side that cannot improve.
hints: Water on a bar depends on the tallest bar to its left and the tallest to its right. How would you get both with two extra arrays?
Keep leftMax and rightMax while two pointers close in. If leftMax <= rightMax, the bar at lo is bounded by leftMax (a taller wall exists on the right), so its water is leftMax - height[lo].
lo = 0, hi = n-1: update the maxes, settle the side with the smaller max, move it. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Bars at the very ends hold no water.
Update the side's max before computing its water so the result is never negative.
A stack-based solution also works, but the two-pointer one is the clearest O(1)-space idea.
